hypothesis: The neuron responds strongly to prominent, smooth curvilinear boundaries and convex 3D forms, specifically spheres, ovoids, circular rims, and broad arcs. The activating features are visually dominated by continuous rounded contours—seen in objects such as eggs, balls, sliced citrus fruit, ceramic bowls, and the arched silhouettes of animals—which typically occupy 30–70% of the image area and are centered or offset to one side. The response is invariant to object identity and surface texture (ranging from glossy enamel and wet fruit pulp to matte stone and fur), as well as color, with activating objects appearing in vibrant red, orange, white, cream, deep brown, or black. These forms are consistently presented against contrasting backgrounds of white, beige, deep blue, or dark shadow, often featuring specular highlights or shading that accentuates their three-dimensional convexity.
